text: Light Agile: 2-week sprints, Kanban, demo to real organisers each sprint
Free tickets and QR check-in ship before paid checkout (ADR 0012)
AI agent threads build the MVP, one per role, orchestrated by PM; tegs reviews and merges
Sign-in asks email only; new accounts give organiser name after the magic link (no account enumeration)
Scale down: no dev AWS account, minimal staging off out of hours; run locally with Docker, no LocalStack
Every PR updates its docs; every role keeps a progress log (working agreement)
Log retention 30 days staging, 90 days production
Rolling sprints: once QA accepts a sprint the next starts at once
Agent setup is provider-independent: AGENTS.md, agents/ briefs, project/ files in the repo
"From A$x" uses the cheapest type on sale, falling back to all types
Security reviews every PR with a migration; nothing joins the merge queue until every reviewer passed it
Event-page HTML stays private, no-store (ADR 0018) with 60 s data cache and /internal/revalidate
project/ and the Claude shared folder sync both ways (scripts/sync-project-files.mjs)
Each review comes from that role's own agent session, not the author's subagents
Template About guidance is placeholder prompts, not prefilled text
Staging API host is api-staging.<domain>; SEC-5 on Cloudflare Free, Pro is tegs's call
Attendee contact email is visible, editable, prefilled with the user's email; publish needs it (SEC-20)
Both AI providers keep working from current state toward the same goal; project/state/graph.jsonl is the shared status source of truth, read first and updated in every PR
Agent PRs need human review and merges
Staging deferred: demos need a public link and real email

Document rotation by key id (a new key at least yearly) in infra/README.md and add the key to the cost estimate (about US$1 a month per environment plus requests).
